newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway asks PLO to explain corruption report.
newsitem.headline: Norway asks PLO to explain corruption report.

text.p: Norway said on Tuesday it had asked the Palestinian Authority to explain allegations that members of the self-rule government had misused public funds.

Norway, which played a leading role in brokering the peace accord between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1993, chairs the Ad-hoc Liaison Committee of countries donating to Palestinian finances.

On Saturday a 600-page report prepared by an auditing office set up by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat showed that some ministers and senior civil servants had squandered or mismanaged $326 million in public funds in 1996.
The report was the first official charge of corruption within the administration since self-rule began in 1994.

"It is important that the Palestinian administration takes this very seriously as it is a question of the Palestinian Authority winning and maintaining the confidence of donor countries," Jan Egeland, Norway's Deputy Foreign Minister, told Reuters.
"We want a translated summary of the report and answers to several questions that we have submitted in writing before the next meeting of the Ad-hoc Liason Committee on June 5 in Washington."
Egeland said he also had approached the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, which both closely follow the development and economy of Palestinian territories, for advice on the report.
Norway has donated around one billion crowns ($141.7 million) to Palestinian areas since 1993 and has budgeted to give a further 400 million crowns in 1997.

"Some of these charges we take very seriously but it is important to underline that all audits and control of donor money indicate that there is little or no apparent misuse or corruption of those funds.
"It's primarily a lack of collection of taxes and customs duties," Egeland said. ($ = 7.057 Norwegian Crowns)
